newsitem.title: USA: Fed's Moskow urges fairer access to home ownership.
newsitem.headline: Fed's Moskow urges fairer access to home ownership.

text.p: Chicago Federal Reserve Bank President Michael Moskow called on local housing professionals to change the way they do business in order to ensure fair treatment of all home buyers.
"We're in a position to implement some real change," he said at a conference of housing industry leaders where he unveiled preliminary recommendations of a Fed-sponsored task force on credit access.
"As much as we can, we want to assure fair and consistent treatment for all home buyers, regardless of where they choose to live, or their race, ethnicity or gender," Moskow said.
"Some of the individual ideas may challenge current thinking on how to do business," Moskow said.

"Some of the recommendations could result in new challenges and potentially some costs. However, these costs should be balanced by the cost of leaving some residents without a full opportunity to build wealth through home ownership."

The task force, formed in September 1996 and comprised of representatives from a broad spectrum of the housing industry, identified the appraisal process, credit reporting, professional and consumer education, and Federal Housing Administration lending issues as points in the home-buying process that may result in unfair treatment.

Actions proposed included reevaluating the appraisal process for properties in blighted areas, mandatory licensing of appraisal professionals, tighter regulation of loan originators, standardizing credit reporting benchmarks, and development of FHA risk-sharing partnerships with private mortgage insurance companies.

Michael Berry, coordinator of the task force project for the Chicago Fed, said some of the plans, such as those involving dissemination of educational publications, were already being carried out, while other proposals could take as long as two years to implement and were subject to revision.
The group's final recommendations are expected to be issued in mid-July.
Moskow, a voting member of the Federal Open Market Committee, did not address U.S. economic or monetary policy issues in his remarks.
